summary: Updates IANA registries so the SEED block cipher can be used for SRTP and SRTCP in Multimedia Internet KEYing (MIKEY). It adds registry values only and is informational.

eli5.summary: A list of allowed code machines needed a new entry. This document adds the SEED cipher to the list so voice and video encryption can use it.

subtitle: Registers code points so the SEED cipher can be negotiated for SRTP and SRTCP in MIKEY.

tldr.problem: MIKEY, the key management protocol for SRTP, had no code points to say that the SEED block cipher is in use.
tldr.mechanism: IANA amended two MIKEY sub-registries: three SEED modes (SEED-CTR, SEED-CCM, SEED-GCM) were added as encryption algorithms, and SEED-CTR was added as a pseudo-random function.
tldr.outcome: Endpoints can now signal SEED in MIKEY. The document changes registry values only and defines no new protocol.

today: RFC 5748 is an Informational RFC from August 2010. The metadata shows it has not been obsoleted or updated, and it stands as the record of these MIKEY registry additions.

sections.title: Introduction and the SEED Cipher
sections.content:
RFC 5748 updates IANA registries to support the SEED block cipher for the Secure Real-time Transport Protocol (SRTP) and the Secure Real-time Transport Control Protocol (SRTCP) in Multimedia Internet KEYing (MIKEY, RFC 3830).

SEED is a 128-bit symmetric key block cipher developed by KISA (Korea Information Security Agency) and a group of experts since 1998. Its block size and key length are both 128 bits, and it has a 16-round Feistel structure. The RFC says it is a Korean National Industrial Association standard and is widely used in South Korea for electronic commerce and security products such as firewalls and VPNs.
sections.eli5: SEED is a secret-code recipe from Korea. This note tells the key-sharing system that the recipe exists.

sections.title: New MIKEY Payload Code Points
sections.content:
The RFC specifies new code points in the MIKEY payload to indicate SEED for SRTP and SRTCP. There are three modes of running SEED, defined in RFC 5669: SEED-CTR (Counter Mode), SEED-CCM (Counter with CBC-MAC Mode) and SEED-GCM (Galois/Counter Mode).

In the table derived from Table 6.10.1.b of RFC 3830 (SRTP encryption algorithm), the existing values are NULL 0, AES-CM 1 and AES-F8 2. The new values are SEED-CTR 3, SEED-CCM 4 and SEED-GCM 5. In the table derived from Table 6.10.1.d (SRTP PRF), AES-CM is 0 and SEED-CTR is the new value 1.
sections.eli5: Each cipher gets a number on a menu. SEED gets three new numbers for its three ways of working, and one more on a second menu.

sections.title: Security and IANA Actions
sections.content:
The security section says no security problem has been found on SEED. It states that SEED is secure against all known attacks including differential cryptanalysis, linear cryptanalysis and related key attacks, and that the only known attack is an exhaustive search for the key. It points readers to the KISA self evaluation report for more.

IANA has amended the indicated sub-registries in the MIKEY Payload Name registry as described above.
sections.eli5: The authors say nobody has found a way to break the recipe except by trying every key. The librarians have written the new numbers in the list.
